title: Solstice Retail private deployment proposal - TF module checklist & upgrade plan (draft)
content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:

This draft proposes a phased private deployment for Solstice Retail (regional retail POS and analytics workloads). Goal: provide a VPC-hosted Redwood Private control plane with on-prem inference/edge clusters in two regions (east/west) behind a central management VPC, with predictable latency (95p token latency < 120ms for 2k concurrent sessions), and an upgrade/rollback path for both Terraform modules and runtime images.

Key decisions recommended here (subject to customer signoff):
- Use k8s-managed inference (k3s or k8s distro TBD) for ease of operator UX, with dedicated GPU node pools per region.
- Terraform modularization: use separate modules for networking, k8s cluster, gpu-pool, kms-integration, and storage; pin provider versions and add automated module test plan.
- Staged rollout: dev -> canary -> production with automated health checks and traffic-splitting.

CUSTOMER CONSTRAINTS / CONTEXT:
- Solstice has two datacenters (IAD and SJC) with on-prem racks. They already run core infra (AD, internal k8s) and have a Palo Alto firewall + dedicated MPLS links to cloud VPCs.
- Data residency: model inference logs must stay in-region for 30 days; audit logs stored in central S3+CloudTrail equivalent.
- Compliance: PCI-scope for payment flows; must use customer KMS for key encryption at rest.
- Expected Q4 traffic: 2k concurrent inference sessions (peak), steady state 400 req/s, median prompt length 120 tokens, median generation 240 tokens.

PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE (high level):
- Management VPC (cloud): Redwood control plane endpoints + S3-compatible object storage for artifacts, central monitoring, and CI runners.
- Edge VPCs (IAD, SJC): Private link/Transit gateway to Management VPC, per-region NAT and egress policies, local EFS/filestore for KV cache snapshots.
- k8s clusters per edge region: node pools
  - GPU inference pool: 4 nodes initially, each with 1x A100-80GB (or customer equivalent), 64 vCPU, 512 GiB RAM (for large-model LLMs)
  - CPU pool (service/sidecars): 6 nodes, 16 vCPU, 64 GiB RAM
  - Spot/burst pool (optional): 2 nodes for batch jobs
- Storage: Ceph/Rook recommended for persistent volumes if customer wants on-prem; fallback to NFS for simpler installs.
- Networking: 10 Gbps interconnect between racks, BGP route exchange to cloud transit; internal load balancer per-region (metal LB or k8s LB).

INITIAL SIZING RATIONALE (starting point, to be validated by perf testing):
- Inference GPU estimate: based on 2k concurrent sessions and per-token latency SLO, start with 4x A100-80GB per region. This supports concurrent KV cache usage and larger context windows.
- CPU/service nodes: sized to handle proxying, batching, and autoscaler pressure.
- Disk: 100 TB usable Ceph cluster per region for model artifacts, KV cache snapshots, and local eval traces (compress at rest).

TERRAFORM MODULE NOTES / CHECKLIST:
- Modules to author/use: network-vpc, transit-gateway (if used), k8s-cluster (cluster provisioning, node pools), gpu-pool (gpu nodegroup resource), kms-integration, object-storage, helm-releases (redwood-runtime, monitoring), security-groups/acl.
- Required provider versions: terraform >=1.5, aws provider pinned at 5.0.x (if cloud resources used), kubernetes provider 2.11.x. Add tidy constraint file in repo.
- Module patterns: keep state per-region in separate backend (S3+locking). Use per-environment workspaces: solstice-dev, solstice-canary, solstice-prod.
- Variables: include explicit instance_type, min/max_node_count, gpu_type, taints/tolerations, kms_key_arn, allowed_cidrs, syslog_endpoint. No secrets in vars; use secret manager references.
- Automated checks:
  - terraform validate and plan in CI on PRs to modules repo
  - unit tests using terratest or kitchen-terraform for network and cluster create/destroy
  - smoke test: deploy a minimal inference job that runs model warmup and returns a checksum within latency bound
- Backwards compatibility: add a migration guide for module API changes. Keep major versioning semver for modules.

SAMPLE TF SNIPPET (reference - keep in modules repo, not applied directly here):
  module "gpu_pool" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//gpu-pool?ref=v1.3.0"
    cluster_name = var.cluster_name
    gpu_instance_type = var.gpu_instance_type
    min_size = var.gpu_min
    max_size = var.gpu_max
    node_labels = { role = "inference-gpu" }
  }

UPGRADE & ROLLOUT PLAN (terraform + runtime):
Phase 0 — Prep (2w):
- Freeze non-critical infra changes. Run terraform plan for current state and record outputs. Create module branch for changes.
- Snapshot PVs, export cluster state (kubectl, etcd snapshot if k8s).
Phase 1 — Dev/Integration (1w):
- Apply updated modules to a dev workspace; run smoke tests and perf benches against smaller model.
Phase 2 — Canary (1w):
- Deploy updated runtime image + tf change to 1 canary node pool (10% traffic) in IAD. Validate latencies, memory, CPU, GPU utilization.
- Run synthetic replay of peak traffic for 1 hour.
Phase 3 — Gradual Prod (2–3w):
- Expand to 50% traffic across both regions. Monitor errors, cost delta, and SLOs. If regressions, automatically rollback via terraform apply to previous module ref and image tag.
Phase 4 — Full rollout & hardening (1w):
- Full scale, finalize runbooks, update module tags.

Rollback mechanics:
- Keep previous runtime image and previous terraform module ref available in artifact registry.
- Maintain an automated rollback pipeline that can switch routes and restore TF state where required.

OPERATIONAL CONSIDERATIONS:
- Monitoring: telemetry pipeline to central observability with per-token traces, per-route latency SLO dashboards, and model-quality regressions.
- SLOs: 95p latency < 120ms, 99p < 300ms (workshop to agree on numbers).
- Alerts: GPU OOM, node failures, autoscaler thrashing, Terraform drift detected (plan != applied).
- Backups: etcd (if k8s control plane customer-managed), Ceph snapshots daily, model artifacts replicated to secondary region.

SECURITY & COMPLIANCE:
- KMS: use customer-managed keys for all model artifacts and snapshot encryption; integrate via terraform kms module.
- Network: restrict egress to approved endpoints; use firewall rules to enforce minimal surface.
- Audit: enable object storage access logs and forward to central SIEM. Retain logs for 90 days locally, 1 year centrally (customer requirement).

COST ESTIMATE (very rough, pre-sales level):
- Initial one-time setup (engineering + runbook + terraform modules): ~4–6 engineer-weeks.
- Infra CAPEX/OPEX: GPUs and telco links dominate. Expected monthly GPU OPEX (two regions, 4x A100 each) ~ $40k–$70k depending on provider/lease. Storage and network add additional ~ $5k–$12k.

ASSUMPTIONS (explicit):
- Customer will provide rack power and 10 Gbps cross-rack connectivity.
- Customer agrees to host model artifacts in a regional object store accessible from edge clusters.
- No requirement to run full control plane on-prem — Redwood control plane will be reachable via private link.
- Model weights are <= 300GB per model (plan capacity accordingly).

RISKS & MITIGATIONS:
- Risk: GPU scarcity / lead time. Mitigation: validate with partner list and offer cloud-bursting fallback.
- Risk: Terraform drift between regions. Mitigation: scheduled drift detection and automatic alerts, restrict direct console changes.
- Risk: Latency higher than expected due to networking. Mitigation: run on-prem network benchmarking and synthetic workload replays during canary.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR SOLSTICE (to resolve before prod rollout):
1) Which k8s distro are they standardized on (RKE, EKS-D, upstream)? (affects module design)
2) Do they want full on-prem control plane or a hybrid with managed control plane in cloud?
3) What exact SLA/retention for audit logs beyond the 30-day regional requirement?
4) Are there any model families that specifically require >80GB GPU memory or multi-GPU sharding?
5) Do they prefer GitOps (ArgoCD) or CI-driven helm releases for runtime updates?

NEXT ACTIONS / OWNER ASSIGNMENTS:
- Asha: finalize TF module checklist and create branch in terraform-modules repo (due 2025-11-18).
- Miguel: schedule perf bench run with sample model (due 2025-11-20).
- Claire: draft runbook for canary/rollback steps and security playbook (due 2025-11-21).
- Solutions Eng: confirm power/network constraints and provide exact rack-level specs (ask customer) (due 2025-11-14).

NOTES / WORKING ITEMS (scratchpad):
- Consider adding optional local KV cache snapshot service to reduce cold start costs.
- Add a terraform import checklist for any previously provisioned network resources.
- Verify KMS key rotation process with Solstice security team.

END OF DRAFT.

This is a working draft intended for internal engineering review and the next call with Solstice Retail. Expect to iterate after the architecture Q&A scheduled 2025-11-10.
